newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Eight Slovak shares to be included in CESI index.
newsitem.headline: Eight Slovak shares to be included in CESI index.

text.p: The eight most heavily- capitalised Slovak shares on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) will be included in the Central European Share Index (CESI), bourse officials said on Wednesday.
"This is a good opportunity for these issues to compare with the most liquid and capitalised shares in Central Europe," BSE chief executive Marian Sasik told a news conference.
Representatives of bourses included in the CESI index decided earlier this week to add stocks from Ljubljana and Bratislava in addition to Budapest, Prague and Warsaw, from October 31.
The increase will bring the total number of issues included on the index to 73 from the current 50 stocks.

Sasik said the Slovak contribution to the CESI index would comprise oil refiner Slovnaft, steel maker VSZ, commercial banks VUB and IRB, oil and gas storage company Nafta, paint producer Chemolak, penicillin-based drug maker Biotika and plastics producer Plastika.
"The significantly lower liquidity of these issues, compared with Budapest, Prague and Warsaw stocks, was the reason for the delay in entering the (CESI) index," Sasik said.

Slovnaft, the heaviest issue, accounting for 30.6 percent of the SAX index and 21.6 percent of the BSE bourse, will account for 2.3 percent of the CESI index, while the entire Slovak participation in the index will be 6.3 percent.
With the inclusion of the new stocks, Budapest will contribute 17.9 percent, Prague 42.5, Warsaw 30.9 and Ljubljana 2.3 percent to the CESI index.
